 by Shri Vivek Shukla - Advocate for the appellant in person.

Shri S K Shrivastava - Government Advocate for the resp
Heard on I.A. No. 22162 of 2025, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of
bail to the appellant Chhotu Tiwari @ Pramod Tiwari.

When this Court asked Shri R.N. Singh, learned Senior Advocate for the appellant as to whether, he would like to withdraw the application, then he said that, he has never withdrawn any Interlocutory Application and would like an order on merits.

Appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 22.07.2025 passed by learned Special Judge (POCSO Act) Rewa in Special Case No. 26/2024, whereby the learned trial Court has convicted the appellant and sentenced as under:
 Conviction Sentence  Section Act Imprisonment Fine if   deposited   3/4 of POCSO Act R.I. for 20 years Rs.1000/- 
 read with Section   376(3) of IPC  341 IPC S.I. for 01 Rs.100   month   506(2) IPC R.I. for 07 years Rs.1000/-

Learned
Sr. Advocate for the appellant submits that, all the witnesses are hostile, there is no proof that victim was minor.
In fact, father of the victim (PW-3) as admitted in his examination in chief that, the age of the victim was 19 years at the time of incident.
He has also stated that, he is not literate and he does not remember the date of birth of the victim.

It is also submitted that, even victim (PW-1) has not supported the prosecution case and has clearly stated that, she does not recognized Chhotu Tiwari @ Pramod Tiwari and Dharamraj Kol @ Letrahe Kol.

She has no information about the incident and thus, reading the evidence of these crucial witnesses alongwith evidence of Dr. Saba Hussain (PW-4) who has stated that she had not found any injury marks on the body and she cannot give any definite opinion about the violation of privacy, so also evidence of Parwati Mishra (PW-5) who has mentioned that, as per Dakhilkharij Register (Ex.P-15 ) date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 10.07.2009, but there is no documentary evidence in support of said date of birth, prays for suspension of sentence on the ground that, appellant is in custody since 1 years and there is no evidence against the present appellant.

Shri S.K. Shrivastava, learned Government Advocate in his turn draws attention of this Court towards the DNA Report (Ex.P-26) issued by State Forensic Science Laboratory, Sagar in which it is mentioned that, vaginal slide of the victim Ex.A (H/691) reveals Y Chromosome STR DNA Profile and the genetic marker alleged found on that slide matches with the Y 3 CRA-8894-2025 Chromosome STR DNA Profile obtained from the blood sample of the accused Chhotu Tiwari @
Pramod Tiwari vide Ex.C (H/693).
Therefore, it is evident that, DNA report is against the appellant Chhotun Tiwari @ Pramod Tiwari.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record.

It is true that,
prosecutrix has turned hostile.
She has not supported the prosecution case.
She has even denied her signatures on various documents like Ex.P-3, Ex.P-4, Ex.P-5 which contained her signatures.

In cross-examination she has stated that, there is party-politics in her village and accused had opposed her family members in the election of Sarpanch, therefore, false report was lodged against the accused persons.
Sister of the victim (PW-2) stated that, she has no information about the case.
She was declared hostile and then she has also not supported the prosecution case.
Father of the victim (PW-3) stated that, victim is his daughter from his first marriage.
His first wife is no more.
age of the victim was stated to be 19 years, but no where in the examination or cross-examination it has come as to at what age he was married and at what age victim was born.
In cross- examination, he stated that he had signed papers at Police Station without reading them.
Dr. Saba Hussain (PW-4) stated that, she cannot give any definite opinion and she had not asked for age determination test for the victim.

sentences.text: Parwati Mishra (PW-5) School Teacher has stated that, the date of birth of the victim to be 10.07.2009, but further stated that, no documentary 4 CRA-8894-2025 evidence was produced at the time of her admission.
However, in her cross- examination, this witness has clearly denied a suggestion that she was making incorrect statement as regard to date of birth of the victim.
She denied suggestion that date of birth of the victim is not 10.07.2009.
When these facts are taken into consideration, there is a corroborative scientific evidence in the form of Ex.P-26 which reveals that, victim had a relationship with the appellant.
This scientific evidence has remained unrebutted.
Thus, it is evident that, victim was giving incorrect ocular evidence, contrary to the scientific evidence.
It is also true that, in the social milieu in which we are growing, there is growing tendency of victim turning hostile for the reasons best known to the victims and their family.

However, when there is corroborative scientific evidence and when there is no independent evidence to suggest that, victim was not a minor at the time of the incidence, we are of the opinion that this is not a fit case to extend benefit of suspension of sentence.
Application (I.A. No. 22162 of 2025) fails and it is dismissed.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (RAMKUMAR  JUDGE JUD  AR Chhotu Tiwari @ Pramod Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7732831/
